title: Bubble and Squeak
subtitle: Crisp fried leftover potato and cabbage cake
excerpt: The best use of leftover roast dinner vegetables: mashed potato and cooked cabbage or Brussels sprouts pressed into a cake and fried in butter until a deep golden crust forms on both sides. Greater than the sum of its leftover parts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bubble and squeak is a dish with roots going back at least to the eighteenth century in Britain, originally made from leftover boiled meat and vegetables. By the twentieth century the meat had been dropped and it had become primarily a leftover potato and cabbage dish, cooked on Boxing Day with the remains of Christmas dinner. The name refers to the sounds the vegetables make as they cook in the pan: they bubble then squeak as the water evaporates.

recipeTools.notes: Non-stick or well-seasoned cast iron works best.

content.text: The crust is the point. Press the mixture firmly into the pan and resist the urge to move it. Leave it on medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until a deep golden crust has formed underneath before attempting to flip. If you move it too early, the crust tears. Some people do the flip as a single cake; others break it up and fry in pieces, which is easier but loses the drama.

Heat half the butter and oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Remove and combine with the potato and cabbage. Season well and mix. The mixture should hold together when pressed.

Add the remaining butter and oil to the pan over medium heat. Add the potato and cabbage mixture and press firmly into an even cake. Cook undisturbed for 8 to 10 minutes until a very deep golden crust has formed on the bottom.

Flip: either slide the cake onto a large plate and invert back into the pan, or break into sections and flip each one. Cook for 6 to 8 more minutes until the other side is equally golden. Serve immediately.
